title: Creative destruction: Human-AI competition in an experimental market
abstract: arXiv:2610.18921v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study two hypotheses for how a human role in production could persist despite growing AI capabilities. Humans might have a durable advantage in taste, designing better products even as AI agents automate routine tasks, or consumers might intrinsically prefer that humans have a hand in production. In our experiment, participants act as producers, designing computer games with an AI coding agent, and as consumers who buy them. Across three studies (N = 1,025), we find no evidence for either hypothesis. Games designed by an AI on its own outperform those of human producers, including both amateurs and professional creatives. Human producers do not anticipate the AI's advantage. Revealing whether a game is human-designed does not raise consumers' willingness to pay for the product.

translated_title: 创造性破坏：实验市场中的人类与AI竞争
translated_abstract: 我们研究了两个假设，探讨在AI能力不断增强的背景下，人类在生产中的角色如何能够持续存在。一种假设是，即使在AI智能体将常规任务自动化的情况下，人类可能在品味方面拥有持久的优势，能够设计出更好的产品；另一种假设是，消费者可能内在地偏好人类参与生产的产品。在我们的实验中，参与者既扮演生产者的角色（使用AI编程智能体设计电脑游戏），也扮演购买这些游戏的消费者。在三项研究（N = 1,025）中，我们没有发现支持任何一种假设的证据。由AI独立设计的游戏表现优于人类生产者设计的游戏，这包括业余爱好者和专业创意人员。人类生产者并未预见到AI的优势。揭示某款游戏是否由人类设计，并不会提高消费者对该产品的支付意愿。
tldr: 通过1025名参与者参与的实验发现，AI独立设计的游戏表现优于人类设计者（包括专业人士）的作品，且消费者并不因产品由人类设计而愿意支付更多，从而否定了人类具有持久品味优势以及消费者偏好人类参与生产这两个假设。
en_tdlr: Experiments with 1,025 participants show that games designed solely by AI outperform those created by human producers (including professionals), and consumers do not pay more for human-designed products, finding no support for either the durable human advantage in taste or the consumer preference for human-made goods hypothesis.
